newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-JOHNSTON LANDS GOLDEN DOUBLE AT GOODWOOD.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-JOHNSTON LANDS GOLDEN DOUBLE AT GOODWOOD.

text.p: Double Trigger, enterprisingly ridden by South African jockey Michael Roberts, led from start to finish to land the Goodwood Cup on Thursday for the second time in his brilliant career.

The 16-1 shot, one of the best stayers of the last decade, came right back to form to beat the hot 5-4 favourite Classic Cliche, brought by Frankie Dettori from the back of the field but still one-and-a-half lengths adrift at the post.
Double Trigger's full brother and stable companion Double Eclipse, who has been plagued by tendon problems, fought gamely to land third place, half a length behind at odds of 12-1.

"We had to throw everything in to this race. It was all or nothing. All the others just ran out of petrol," ebullient Scottish trainer Mark Johnston said after Double Trigger landed the great Goodwood stamina test for the second time in three years.

Double Trigger and Double Eclipse had fought an epic battle against each other in the 1995 Goodwood Cup and Johnston said: "The only way it could have been better today would have been to have first and second again."

Johnston rounded of a memorable afternoon when the 14-1 shot Fly To The Stars was swept to victory in the valuable Golden Mile, which was delayed when faulty starting stalls sprang open and the field had to be recalled.
Daggers Drawn became the 7-1 clear favourite for next year's 2,000 Guineas after a dogged victory by one-and-a-half lengths over 10-1 shot Lord Kintire in the Richmond Stakes.

"It was a nightmare journey there for a while. I had a wall of horses in front of me but the gap opened. There is a God after all," a clearly relieved Kieren Fallon said after finally extricating the colt to win at cramped odds of 13-8 on.

Fallon won Wednesday's group one Sussex Stakes on Ali-Royal but then half an hour later was banned for five days for irresponsible riding after finishing an erratic second on Memorise in the Tote Gold Trophy
One of the big stars on Ladies Day at Glorious Goodwood was Dazzle, who showed a scintillating turn of speed to land the Oaktree Stakes by half a length from the 33-1 shot Unconditional Love.

"I had a few traffic problems but she quickened really good. She has a devastating turn of foot," Northern Irish jockey John Reid said after steering the 11-4 chance to a deceptively comfortable victory that saw her back at her sparkling best.
